dhp360:1: Excellent is restraint of the eye,
dhp360:2: excellent is restraint of the ear,
dhp360:3: excellent is restraint of the nose,
dhp360:4: excellent is restraint of the tongue,
dhp361:1: excellent is restraint of the body,
dhp361:3: excellent is restraint of the mind,
dhp361:4: excellent is restraint in every situation.
dhp361:5: A monk who is restrained in every situation
dhp362:2: speech restrained, restrained to the utmost,
dhp362:4: one who is content like this is called a monk.
dhp363:1: A monk who has a restrained mouth,
dhp363:3: illuminates the meaning and the Dhamma,
dhp363:4: and their speech is like honey.
dhp364:1: Appreciating the Dhamma, approving of the Dhamma,
dhp364:4: a monk does not fall away from the true Dhamma.
dhp365:1: One should not disdain what one has,
dhp365:2: nor envy what belongs to others;
dhp365:3: a monk who envies the belongings of others
dhp366:1: Even if a monk has little,
dhp366:2: but does not disdain what he has,
dhp366:4: the one who lives with purity and diligence.
dhp367:1: When there is nothing whatsoever in mind and body
dhp367:3: and one does not sorrow on account of the unpleasant,
dhp367:4: then one can be called a monk.
